title: Leaders Spread Behaviors Like Germs
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article uses the neuroscience of mirror neurons to explain why team members unconsciously mimic the emotions, goals, and behaviors of leaders they respect. It draws a direct line from contagious moods at a concert or sporting event to contagious workplace behaviors like decisiveness, risk-taking, and active listening, arguing that leaders shape team behavior far more through what they do than through what they say. The piece calls on leaders to stay especially conscious of what they decline, avoid, ignore, and dismiss, since those choices are being observed and copied just as readily as their positive actions.
points: Mirror neurons allow people to unconsciously simulate and adopt the emotions and behaviors of others around them.
This mimicry extends beyond emotion to goals, decisiveness, risk-taking, and even rule-breaking.
Team members are heavily shaped by what leaders actually do, not just by what they say or suggest.
The most precise and consistent leader behaviors are the most likely to be adopted by others.
Leaders should be especially conscious of what they decline, avoid, or dismiss, since those choices are observed and copied too.
quotes: Mirror neurons in the brain allow us to realistically simulate the actions performed by others and the results they experience.
We catch and mimic the emotions of others quite easily. Emotions are highly contagious and commonly lead to shared experiences and reactions.
Team members are heavily influenced by what leaders do, not just by what they say or suggest.
Leaders are always on stage for the smallest things they do.
They remind themselves daily that their behaviors spread like fast-growing roots on the tree of imitation.
